message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on decoden craft kits. Goods put up as a set for retail sale are classified under GRI 3(b) by the component that gives the set its essential character. The candidate components are:

- The plastic case, classified in 3926.90 (other articles of plastics) or 4202.92 (carrying cases with an outer surface of plastic sheeting).
- The plastic charms, beads and crystals, classified in 3926.40 (statuettes and other ornamental articles of plastic) or 3926.90.
- The adhesive, classified in 3506.10 (adhesives put up for retail sale in packages of no more than 1 kg).

The user decorates the case with the embellishments, so the decorative items likely give the kit its essential character. Other decoden kit rulings I recall classified such kits under 9503.00.00 (toys) or 3926.40.00. Here the case is the item being decorated, and the embellishments are the main part of the craft.

My best recollection is that CBP classified the kits under 3926.40.0090 as ornamental articles of plastic, with the decorative plastic pieces as the essential character. Another possibility is 3926.90.9990 for the case. I'm going with 3926.40.0090.

3926.40.0090 is the "Other" subheading under statuettes and other ornamental articles. The HTSUS has 3926.40.0010 for statuettes and ornaments and 3926.40.0090 for other.

{"hts_code": "3926.40.0090", "reason": "The kit is a set under GRI 3(b), and the decorative plastic charms, beads and crystals give it its essential character, so it is classified as other ornamental articles of plastic."}
